title: 0x and 0o integers of 2^64 are exact or refused, never rounded
notes: The core schema reads a plain scalar that matches `0x[0-9a-fA-F]+` as a hexadecimal integer and one that matches `0o[0-7]+` as an octal integer, and gives neither an upper bound (section 10.3.2). Turning one into a float, a string or a wrapped 64-bit number changes the data without a word. YAML 1.2.2 section 10.2.1.3 lets a processor reject an integer it cannot hold as an error. The kit therefore accepts the exact integer or a refusal (strict: a `limit` error). Truncating or converting the value fails, because the kit cannot see a warning. A crash, a hang, a wrong result, or more than the stated time or memory fails. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. Both values are 2^64, the first one that does not fit an unsigned 64-bit integer; longer forms are in `schema/core-integers-beyond-64-bits`.

provenance.reference: Hexadecimal and octal integers past 64 bits read as strings, floats or wrapped numbers in several libraries.
